title: Martin Van Buren — The Life, The Rise, And The Legacy #Shorts
description:
The last chapter of Martin Van Buren was written long after the fame. Martin Van Buren (December 5, 1782 – July 24, 1862) was the eighth president of the United States, serving from 1837 to 1841. He co-founded the Democratic Party with Andrew Jackson and became Jackson's vice president from 1833 to 1837.

The life of Martin Van Buren begins far from where the story usually starts. The Regency relied on a coalition of small farmers, but also enjoyed support from the Tammany Hall machine in New York City. During this era, Van Buren largely determined Tammany Hall's political policy for New York's Democratic-Republicans.
